column1: Blank in the cycle-time and counter columns = the .dtx in that backup carries only the SHIPPED DEFAULTS (Last 4.9 s, 10-sample avg 6.22 s), not a measurement. Ordinary VAL3 globals reach a backup only when the application data is SAVED FROM SP2 first - which happened once, before the 17h43m pull. '10-sample avg' is the mean of the 10-slot _nCycleTime ring, NOT a run average - the 145-pick run's own average is the 1000-window figure, 6.63 s.

File size is a build fingerprint only until SP2 re-saves: the 17h43m save re-sorted <Local> declarations alphabetically and re-indented some loop bodies, changing sizes with no code change. It stripped all 17 .dtx comments, and preserved the .pgx comments exactly (tkCycle 519, tkBeltScan 249, both unchanged) - so documentation belongs in the .pgx files, never the .dtx.

Value elements and .dtx comments are blank where that backup is held as a zip whose .dtx is not extracted in the analysis folder - the byte size is still known. Log events is blank for 17h43m, whose logArchive.zip is a OneDrive cloud-only placeholder; hydrate it (right-click > Always keep on this device) and re-run parse_backups.py to fill it in.

Log events = unique entries recovered from that backup's logArchive.zip. The CS9 log is cumulative, so a newer backup contains the older entries too; the climb 4,375 -> 5,122 is new activity, not new history.
